title: Okabe and City
statementMd:
Okabe likes to be able to walk through his city on a path lit by street lamps. That way, he doesn't get beaten up by schoolchildren.

Okabe's city is represented by a 2D grid of cells. Rows are numbered from $1$ to $*n*$ from top to bottom, and columns are numbered $1$ to $*m*$ from left to right. Exactly $*k*$ cells in the city are lit by a street lamp. It's guaranteed that the top-left cell is lit.

Okabe starts his walk from the top-left cell, and wants to reach the bottom-right cell. Of course, Okabe will only walk on lit cells, and he can only move to adjacent cells in the up, down, left, and right directions. However, Okabe can also temporarily light all the cells in any single row or column at a time if he pays $1$ coin, allowing him to walk through some cells not lit initially.

Note that Okabe can only light a single row or column at a time, and has to pay a coin every time he lights a new row or column. To change the row or column that is temporarily lit, he must stand at a cell that is lit initially. Also, once he removes his temporary light from a row or column, all cells in that row/column not initially lit are now not lit.

Help Okabe find the minimum number of coins he needs to pay to complete his walk!

## Input

The first line of input contains three space-separated integers $*n*$, $*m*$, and $*k*$ ($2 ≤ *n*, *m*, *k* ≤ 10^{4}$).

Each of the next $*k*$ lines contains two space-separated integers $*r*_{*i*}$ and $*c*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$, $1 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ *m*$) — the row and the column of the $*i*$-th lit cell.

It is guaranteed that all $*k*$ lit cells are distinct. It is guaranteed that the top-left cell is lit.

## Output

Print the minimum number of coins Okabe needs to pay to complete his walk, or `-1` if it's not possible.

## Note

In the first sample test, Okabe can take the path ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fd8d0b719801e9cfe8f6be340d76a554f6ffb66b.png), paying only when moving to $(2, 3)$ and $(4, 4)$.

In the fourth sample, Okabe can take the path ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a91fe94734a09a4ba86d66070aa8cbeacdb2279f.png) ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2ee6688fe94ce8e9a746b8e479e906fe25ff4d86.png), paying when moving to $(1, 2)$, $(3, 4)$, and $(5, 4)$.
statementZhMd:
Okabe 喜欢沿着由路灯照亮的道路穿过城市。这样一来，他就不会被小学生打。

Okabe 所在的城市由一个二维网格表示。行从上到下编号为 $1$ 到 $*n*$，列从左到右编号为 $1$ 到 $*m*$。城市中恰好有 $*k*$ 个格子被路灯照亮。保证左上角的格子是亮着的。

Okabe 从左上角的格子出发，希望到达右下角的格子。当然，Okabe 只会在亮着的格子上行走，并且只能向上、下、左、右四个方向移动。不过，如果支付 $1$ 枚硬币，Okabe 还可以暂时点亮任意一整行或一整列中的所有格子，从而经过一些初始时没有被点亮的格子。

注意，Okabe 一次只能点亮一行或一列，并且每次点亮新的一行或一列时都必须支付一枚硬币。若要更换暂时点亮的行或列，他必须站在一个初始时就被点亮的格子上。此外，一旦他取消对某行或某列的临时照明，该行或该列中所有初始时没有被点亮的格子都会重新变为不亮。

请帮助 Okabe 求出完成这次行走所需支付的最少硬币数！

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含三个用空格分隔的整数 $*n*$、$*m*$ 和 $*k*$（$2 ≤ *n*, *m*, *k* ≤ 10^{4}$）。

接下来的 $*k*$ 行中，每行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 $*r*_{*i*}$ 和 $*c*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *r*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$，$1 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ *m*$），表示第 $*i*$ 个被点亮格子的行号和列号。

保证这 $*k*$ 个被点亮的格子互不相同。保证左上角的格子被点亮。

## 输出格式

输出 Okabe 完成行走所需支付的最少硬币数；如果无法完成，则输出 `-1`。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，Okabe 可以沿着路径 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/fd8d0b719801e9cfe8f6be340d76a554f6ffb66b.png) 行走，只需在移动到 $(2, 3)$ 和 $(4, 4)$ 时支付硬币。

在第四个样例中，Okabe 可以沿着路径 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a91fe94734a09a4ba86d66070aa8cbeacdb2279f.png) ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/2ee6688fe94ce8e9a746b8e479e906fe25ff4d86.png) 行走，只需在移动到 $(1, 2)$、$(3, 4)$ 和 $(5, 4)$ 时支付硬币。
